chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Ahmad ibn Idris, from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar and Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, all of them from Safwan ibn Yahya, from 'Isa ibn al-Qasim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Indeed, a group from Banu Hashim came to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and asked him to appoint them over the alms-tax of livestock, saying: 'Let us have this share that Allah, Exalted and Majestic, has designated for those who work over it, for we are more deserving of it.' So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'O Banu Abd al-Muttalib, indeed alms-tax (sadaqah) is not permissible for me nor for you, but I have been promised intercession.'

Then Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Bear witness that I have indeed been promised it. So what do you think, O Banu Abd al-Muttalib, when I take hold of the ring of the door of Paradise, do you see me preferring anyone else over you?'

key_terms.بِحَلْقَةِ بَابِ الْجَنَّةِ: by the ring of the door of Paradise
key_terms.لِلْعَامِلِينَ عَلَيْهَا: for those who work over it

ai.seo_question: Why is zakat forbidden for the Prophet and his family according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from Tahdhib al-Ahkam clarifies the distinction between the Prophet's personal exemption from sadaqah and the broader prohibition for Banu Hashim, contrasting their material exclusion with the spiritual promise of intercession (shafa'ah). It highlights the Shia understanding that the Ahl al-Bayt's reward is not worldly wealth but a unique status in the Hereafter, where the Prophet will prioritize them at the Gates of Paradise. This narrative reinforces the concept of 'shafa'ah' as a specific, guaranteed privilege for the Prophet and his progeny, distinct from general intercession.
